summary: Chicago Public Schools supports preserving existing E-Rate discount rates and eligibility criteria to ensure affordability and avoid additional administrative costs. Chicago Public Schools opposes changes to E-Rate decisions that tie them to educational outcomes, arguing that misclassifying large urban districts as well-resourced ignores the high cost of delivering technology across numerous facilities. The school district highlights the cost savings and benefits of dark fiber for broadband connectivity, urging the FCC to protect existing infrastructure projects and transition to permanent Category Two eligibility for cybersecurity infrastructure. The district emphasizes the importance of network reliability and the need to prevent cyber threats from disrupting essential services. The school district argues against the proposed changes to E-Rate, stating that retaining full eligibility for Pre-K and Head Start programs without requiring cost-allocation filings would be beneficial for budgetary reasons and avoid administrative burdens.
